title: How to live with bipolar disorder, with David Miklowitz, PhD, and Terri Cheney

sentences.en: Up to 4% of people in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国，有多达4%的人口

sentences.en: live with bipolar disorder, what used to be called manic depression.
sentences.zh: 患有双相障碍，也就是过去所说的躁郁症。

sentences.en: But as common as this mood disorder is, it is also often misunderstood and misdiagnosed.
sentences.zh: 但尽管这种心境障碍很常见，它却经常被误解和误诊。

sentences.en: Indeed, many people with bipolar disorder wait years between experiencing their first symptoms and receiving an accurate diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多双相障碍患者从出现最初症状到获得准确诊断，往往要等待数年之久。

sentences.en: And the general public perception that bipolar disorder is always severe and untreatable is both harmful and out of date.
sentences.zh: 而公众普遍认为双相障碍总是很严重且无法治愈，这种看法既有害又过时。

sentences.en: Over the past few decades, researchers have made great strides in understanding how to recognize, diagnose, and treat bipolar disorder with both psychotherapy and medications.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几十年里，研究人员在了解如何通过心理治疗和药物来识别、诊断和治疗双相障碍方面取得了巨大进展。

sentences.en: So what are the symptoms of bipolar disorder and how is it diagnosed?
sentences.zh: 那么，双相障碍的症状有哪些？它是如何被诊断出来的呢？

sentences.en: At what age do symptoms usually first appear?
sentences.zh: 症状通常在什么年龄首次出现？

sentences.en: What does bipolar disorder look like in children and teens versus adults?
sentences.zh: 儿童、青少年和成人的双相障碍表现有何不同？

sentences.en: What treatments are available?
sentences.zh: 有哪些治疗方法？

sentences.en: And is bipolar disorder linked to creativity or is that just a myth?
sentences.zh: 双相障碍与创造力有关吗？还是这仅仅是一个神话？

sentences.en: Is it genetic or something that people develop as a result of trauma?
sentences.zh: 它是遗传性的，还是人们因创伤而产生的疾病？

sentences.en: And what are researchers learning about helping people with bipolar disorder manage it and live healthy, productive lives?
sentences.zh: 研究人员在帮助双相障碍患者管理病情并过上健康、充实的生活方面有哪些新发现？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听美国心理学会的旗舰播客《心理学谈话》，我们将探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们邀请了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: The first is Dr. David Miklowitz, a clinical psychologist and professor in the Department of Psychiatry at the University of California, Los Angeles, Semel Institute.
sentences.zh: 第一位是临床心理学家、加州大学洛杉矶分校塞梅尔研究所精神病学系教授大卫·米克洛维茨（Dr. David Miklowitz）博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Miklowitz treats and conducts research with people who have bipolar disorder and their families.
sentences.zh: 米克洛维茨博士致力于治疗双相障碍患者及其家属，并开展相关研究。

sentences.en: Much of his research focuses on families' psychoeducational treatments for childhood-onset bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 他的大部分研究集中在针对儿童期发病的双相障碍的家庭心理教育治疗上。

sentences.en: He's won many awards for his research and has published more than 300 research articles and eight books, including guides to bipolar disorder for both clinicians and patients.
sentences.zh: 他因研究成果荣获多项大奖，发表了300多篇研究论文，并著有八本书，其中包括供临床医生和患者参考的双相障碍指南。

sentences.en: His best-selling book, The Bipolar Disorder Survival Guide, is in its third edition with more than 300,000 copies in print.
sentences.zh: 他的畅销书《双相障碍生存指南》（The Bipolar Disorder Survival Guide）已出到第三版，印刷量超过30万册。

sentences.en: Our second guest is writer and mental health advocate, Terry Cheney.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是作家兼心理健康倡导者特里·切尼（Terry Cheney）。

sentences.en: Ms. Cheney has chronicled her lifelong experience with bipolar disorder in three books,
sentences.zh: 切尼女士在三本书中记录了她与双相障碍相伴一生的经历，

sentences.en: Manic, a memoir, The Dark Side of Innocence Growing Up Bipolar, and her recent Modern Madness and Owner's Manual.
sentences.zh: 分别是回忆录《躁狂》（Manic）、《纯真的阴暗面：双相成长记》（The Dark Side of Innocence Growing Up Bipolar），以及她最近的作品《现代疯狂与使用手册》（Modern Madness and Owner's Manual）。

sentences.en: A 2008 column that she wrote for the New York Times about living with bipolar disorder was adapted into an episode of the Netflix television series, Modern Love.
sentences.zh: 她2008年为《纽约时报》撰写的一篇关于双相障碍生活的专栏文章，被改编成了Netflix电视剧《现代爱情》（Modern Love）中的一集。

sentences.en: Before becoming a writer and mental health advocate, she worked for many years as an entertainment attorney in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 在成为作家和心理健康倡导者之前，她曾在洛杉矶担任多年的娱乐律师。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 感谢二位今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: It's great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Let's start with the basics, Dr. Miklowitz.
sentences.zh: 让我们从基础知识开始吧，米克洛维茨博士。

sentences.en: Could you give us an overview of how bipolar disorder is defined and diagnosed?
sentences.zh: 您能给我们概述一下双相障碍是如何定义和诊断的吗？

sentences.en: I know there are several different subtypes in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders.
sentences.zh: 我知道在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》中，它有几种不同的亚型。

sentences.en: What do they have in common and how are they different?
sentences.zh: 它们有什么共同点，又有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Bipolar disorder used to be called manic depression.
sentences.zh: 双相障碍过去被称为躁郁症。

sentences.en: It's one of our oldest psychiatric disorders.
sentences.zh: 它是我们最古老的精神疾病之一。

sentences.en: It's been recognized really since the 1800s, perhaps even before.
sentences.zh: 实际上自19世纪以来，甚至可能更早，它就已经被人们所认识了。

sentences.en: And it's characterized by very severe mood swings from what we call mania to depression.
sentences.zh: 它的特点是情绪会在我们所说的“躁狂”和“抑郁”之间发生非常剧烈的波动。

sentences.en: In states of mania, people have a couple of weeks or maybe even months of having very high mood or extreme irritability.
sentences.zh: 在躁狂状态下，人们会有几周甚至几个月的时间处于极度高涨或极度易怒的情绪中。

sentences.en: Their moods really are kind of out of control.
sentences.zh: 他们的情绪确实有点失控。

sentences.en: With that is kind of a sped up energetic feeling.
sentences.zh: 伴随而来的是一种加速的、充满活力的感觉。

sentences.en: They feel like they have lots of energy.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己精力充沛。

sentences.en: They don't feel as much need to sleep.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得对睡眠的需求减少了。

sentences.en: They can go nights without sleeping or sleep very little.
sentences.zh: 他们可以彻夜不眠，或者睡眠极少。

sentences.en: Grandiose ideas or what we call inflated self-esteem, the sort of sense of having extra powers or even believing that you're a famous person.
sentences.zh: 夸大的想法，或者我们所说的“自尊心膨胀”，即感觉自己拥有超能力，甚至相信自己是个名人。

sentences.en: Hypersexuality is often goes along with it as excessive sex drive or impulsive behavior like spending.
sentences.zh: 性欲亢进通常也伴随其中，表现为性冲动过强或冲动行为，比如乱花钱。

sentences.en: Speaking very faSt.
sentences.zh: 说话速度非常快。

sentences.en: It's a very sped up state.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常加速的状态。

sentences.en: Now, those episodes alternate with depressions, which most of us are more familiar with.
sentences.zh: 这些发作期会与抑郁期交替出现，而抑郁期是我们大多数人比较熟悉的。

sentences.en: But it's more than just sadness.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是悲伤。

sentences.en: It's depressed mood, depressive clinical states involving slowed down, fatigued, excessive sleeping or having insomnia, perhaps depression, loss of interest in things,
sentences.zh: 它是抑郁心境，临床抑郁状态涉及动作迟缓、疲劳、睡眠过多或失眠，可能还有抑郁、对事物失去兴趣，

sentences.en: nothing is fun, loss of concentration, and often suicidal thinking or behavior.
sentences.zh: 觉得什么都没意思、注意力不集中，并且经常有自杀的想法或行为。

sentences.en: And people with bipolar disorder alternate between those two extremes.
sentences.zh: 双相障碍患者就在这两个极端之间交替。

sentences.en: There are people who have both at the same time.
sentences.zh: 也有人会同时出现这两种状态。

sentences.en: We call them mixed if they've had both mania and depression at the same time.
sentences.zh: 如果他们同时经历躁狂和抑郁，我们称之为“混合状态”。

sentences.en: We also have some people would say it's a milder form, although that's some question of debate.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一些人会说这是一种较轻的形式，尽管这还有待商榷。

sentences.en: Bipolar 2 disorder, which is a variation between severe depression and hypomania.
sentences.zh: 双相II型障碍，这是严重抑郁和轻躁狂之间的一种变体。

sentences.en: Hypomania being less severe version of mania, less likely to cause impairment, even though the same symptoms may be there.
sentences.zh: 轻躁狂是躁狂的较轻版本，不太可能导致功能受损，尽管可能存在相同的症状。

sentences.en: So we have we think it's about two to three percent of the population that has this disorder in some form.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为大约有2%到3%的人口以某种形式患有这种疾病。

sentences.en: Does that sound right to you, Miss Cheney?
sentences.zh: 切尼女士，这听起来对吗？

sentences.en: And what does it feel like to cycle between these mood states?
sentences.zh: 在这些情绪状态之间循环是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I think that covered most of the territory.
sentences.zh: 我想这涵盖了大部分情况。

sentences.en: I would add that in mania, it's not the fun, euphoric, exciting state most people think it is.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，在躁狂状态下，这并不是大多数人认为的那种有趣、欣快、令人兴奋的状态。

sentences.en: There's a lot of agitation and irritability that goes along with it, and certainly with mixed states as well.
sentences.zh: 它伴随着大量的焦虑和易怒，当然混合状态也是如此。

sentences.en: I think that mostly people understand depression better than mania.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对抑郁的理解比对躁狂的理解要好。

sentences.en: So that's the big mystery is what is mania really like?
sentences.zh: 所以最大的谜团是：躁狂到底是什么样的？

sentences.en: What do we know about the causes of bipolar disorder?
sentences.zh: 关于双相障碍的成因，我们了解多少？

sentences.en: Is it, as I mentioned in the intro, I was asking whether it's genetic or can it be precipitated by some kind of a traumatic life experience or childhood experience?
sentences.zh: 正如我在开场白中提到的，我想问的是，它是遗传的，还是可能由某种创伤性生活经历或童年经历引发的？

sentences.en: Or is it something that runs in families?
sentences.zh: 或者它是家族遗传的吗？

sentences.en: I would say this.
sentences.zh: 我会这样说。

sentences.en: It is a combination of genetic, biological and social.
sentences.zh: 它是遗传、生物和社会因素的结合。

sentences.en: It certainly runs in families.
sentences.zh: 它确实具有家族聚集性。

sentences.en: People run, people inherit a predisposition to bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 人们遗传了双相障碍的易感性。

sentences.en: They don't necessarily have bipolar people in their family that they can identify.
sentences.zh: 他们不一定能确定家族中有患双相障碍的人。

sentences.en: But often there's somebody in the family tree who's had this disorder.
sentences.zh: 但通常在家族树中会有人患有这种疾病。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's a grandparent.
sentences.zh: 有时是祖父母。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's a parent.
sentences.zh: 有时是父母。

sentences.en: And certainly depression also runs in those families.
sentences.zh: 当然，抑郁症也在这些家庭中流行。

sentences.en: So we have good reason to believe it's genetic.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有充分的理由相信它是遗传的。

sentences.en: And some genetic markers have been found, DNA markers.
sentences.zh: 而且已经发现了一些遗传标记，即DNA标记。

sentences.en: There is also evidence for environmental stress triggering those vulnerabilities.
sentences.zh: 也有证据表明环境压力会触发这些脆弱性。

sentences.en: So people who have the vulnerability may have a childhood experience.
sentences.zh: 所以那些有易感性的人可能会有某种童年经历。

sentences.en: It may trigger the psychophysiological dysfunctions that are characteristic of the disorder.
sentences.zh: 这可能会触发该疾病特有的心理生理功能障碍。

sentences.en: So we're sort of thinking about it as you come into this world with a vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 所以我们倾向于认为，你带着这种脆弱性来到这个世界。

sentences.en: Certain life events can make it worse or trigger it in the first place or make it more recurrent.
sentences.zh: 某些生活事件可能会使情况恶化，或者从一开始就触发它，或者使其更频繁地复发。

sentences.en: So both are important.
sentences.zh: 所以两者都很重要。

sentences.en: Does that ring true for you, Terry?
sentences.zh: 特里，这听起来真实吗？

sentences.en: Are there people in your family who have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder in addition to you?
sentences.zh: 除了你之外，你的家人中还有人被诊断出患有双相障碍吗？

sentences.en: No one in my family that I'm aware of was diagnosed with bipolar disorder, which doesn't mean they didn't have it.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，我的家人中没有人被诊断出患有双相障碍，但这并不意味着他们没有患病。

sentences.en: They just weren't diagnosed because it wasn't paid much attention to previously.
sentences.zh: 他们只是没有被诊断出来，因为以前人们对此关注不多。

sentences.en: But I certainly felt that I had it even as a very young child.
sentences.zh: 但我确实觉得我即使在很小的时候就患有这种病。

sentences.en: I had a suicide attempt at age seven.
sentences.zh: 我在七岁时就尝试过自杀。

sentences.en: So for me, it went way back.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这由来已久。

sentences.en: So at what age do people tend to first experience symptoms of bipolar disorder?
sentences.zh: 那么人们通常在什么年龄首次出现双相障碍的症状？

sentences.en: David, maybe you could answer that one.
sentences.zh: 大卫，也许你可以回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that's been a topic of some debate in the last couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 这在过去几十年里一直是一个争论的话题。

sentences.en: We used to think bipolar disorder didn't have onset until the early 20s.
sentences.zh: 我们过去认为双相障碍直到20岁出头才会发病。

sentences.en: But now more and more university sites and clinics are seeing this disorder in adolescents and even sometimes in kids.
sentences.zh: 但现在越来越多的大学站点和诊所开始在青少年甚至有时在儿童身上看到这种疾病。

sentences.en: That's where there's the biggest debate is, is this, you know, does this occur in young children?
sentences.zh: 这就是最大的争议所在：这种病在幼儿身上会发生吗？

sentences.en: And some people say it happens regularly.
sentences.zh: 有些人说它经常发生。

sentences.en: Some people say it's very rare.
sentences.zh: 有些人说它非常罕见。

sentences.en: My own experience is it's pretty rare, but it does occur.
sentences.zh: 我个人的经验是它相当罕见，但确实会发生。

sentences.en: Where we see more of it is in adolescence, where people have their first manic episode or their first depressive episode.
sentences.zh: 我们更多地是在青春期看到这种情况，那时人们经历了第一次躁狂发作或第一次抑郁发作。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's that they had a mild depressive episode in adolescence and then a more severe mania when they become young adults.
sentences.zh: 有时是因为他们在青春期有过轻微的抑郁发作，然后在成年早期出现了更严重的躁狂。

sentences.en: Or they have one of these hypomanic episodes in childhood and then a major depression during adolescence.
sentences.zh: 或者他们在童年时期有过轻躁狂发作，然后在青春期出现了重度抑郁。

sentences.en: So the average age of onset is nationally is about 18, but there's quite a bit of variability anywhere from 14, you know, at the low end, 12, at the high end, 25.
sentences.zh: 所以全国平均发病年龄约为18岁，但变异性很大，低至14岁、12岁，高至25岁都有可能。

sentences.en: And how do you treat children with something like bipolar disorder?
sentences.zh: 那么你们如何治疗患有双相障碍之类的儿童呢？

sentences.en: I mean, one of the classic treatments, and we'll get into this a little bit more, is drugs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，经典的治疗方法之一，我们稍后会详细讨论，就是药物治疗。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's very controversial as to whether you give drugs to very young children.
sentences.zh: 但是，给幼儿用药是非常有争议的。

sentences.en: Well, if it's a very young child, we don't come in with all guns blazing, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果是非常小的孩子，我们不会“火力全开”，可以这么说。

sentences.en: You don't necessarily give the strongest medications.
sentences.zh: 你不一定要使用最强效的药物。

sentences.en: If it's unquestionably bipolar disorder, you know, you're really seeing a kid that needs to be in the hospital or he or she is suicidal or they're, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果毫无疑问是双相障碍，你知道，你看到的是一个需要住院的孩子，或者他/她有自杀倾向，或者他们，你知道，

sentences.en: unable to function in the home or at school.
sentences.zh: 无法在家里或学校正常生活。

sentences.en: You might try a medicine, which might be an antipsychotic or it might be a mood stabilizer.
sentences.zh: 你可能会尝试一种药物，可能是抗精神病药，也可能是情绪稳定剂。

sentences.en: But generally, we like to not jump in with the heaviest medications at firSt.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，我们不喜欢一开始就使用最重的药物。

sentences.en: By adolescence, when the disorder is kind of declared itself and we're already seeing cycling patterns, that's when we're usually introducing a mood stabilizer or an antipsychotic.
sentences.zh: 到了青春期，当疾病已经显现，我们已经看到循环模式时，通常会引入情绪稳定剂或抗精神病药。

sentences.en: And it's a hard emotional question to address for the patient,
sentences.zh: 对于患者来说，这是一个很难解决的情感问题，

sentences.en: for the kid and the family about taking medicines and how long do you take them for and what happens if you don't take them.
sentences.zh: 对于孩子和家庭来说，关于服用药物、服用多久以及如果不服用会发生什么，都是如此。

sentences.en: Some people prefer the kind of wait and see.
sentences.zh: 有些人更喜欢“观望”的态度。

sentences.en: Let's see what happens over time.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看随着时间的推移会发生什么。

sentences.en: But if the kid is being very self-destructive, then you may not have that option.
sentences.zh: 但如果孩子有很强的自毁倾向，那么你可能就没有那种选择了。

sentences.en: And it's very tough on parents when they have to make that decision.
sentences.zh: 当父母必须做出那个决定时，这对他们来说非常艰难。

sentences.en: So let me ask you, Terry, how old were you when you first experienced symptoms?
sentences.zh: 那么让我问你，特里，你第一次出现症状时多大？

sentences.en: I mean, you mentioned a suicide attempt at seven.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你提到了七岁时的一次自杀尝试。

sentences.en: Was that really the onset?
sentences.zh: 那真的是发病吗？

sentences.en: And then how long did it take for you to actually get diagnosed and get help?
sentences.zh: 然后你花了多长时间才真正得到诊断并获得帮助？

sentences.en: Well, I had classic symptoms of cycling throughout my childhood where I would, particularly with depression, where I would fall into these states where I couldn't get out of bed,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在整个童年时期都有典型的循环症状，特别是抑郁症，我会陷入这些无法起床的状态，

sentences.en: couldn't go to school.
sentences.zh: 无法去上学。

sentences.en: Those would last a few weeks and then I'd come roaring back to life and do all these extra credit reports and all to make up what I'd missed.
sentences.zh: 这些状态会持续几周，然后我会充满活力地回来，做所有额外的学分报告来弥补我错过的东西。

sentences.en: So it took, unfortunately, until I was 34 years old before I got a diagnosis and it was the wrong diagnosis, as so often happens.
sentences.zh: 所以不幸的是，直到我34岁时才得到诊断，而且是错误的诊断，这种情况经常发生。

sentences.en: It was major depression because that's how I presented to the doctor.
sentences.zh: 那是重度抑郁症，因为这就是我向医生呈现的样子。

sentences.en: You don't go in when you're manic because you're feeling so high.
sentences.zh: 你不会在躁狂时去看医生，因为你感觉太好了。

sentences.en: So all the doctor saw was my depression and treated me for that.
sentences.zh: 所以医生看到的只是我的抑郁，并以此治疗我。

sentences.en: Was that at least helpful?
sentences.zh: 那至少有帮助吗？

sentences.en: At the time, it did help somewhat, yes.
sentences.zh: 当时确实有一定帮助，是的。

sentences.en: But it also, I think, triggered.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为它触发了（病情）。

sentences.en: I was on an antidepressant and I think it triggered cycling, which can happen if you're not treated properly with a mood stabilizer.
sentences.zh: 我当时在服用抗抑郁药，我认为它触发了循环，如果你没有用情绪稳定剂进行适当治疗，这种情况就会发生。

sentences.en: So, David, what are the effective treatments?
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，有效的治疗方法是什么？

sentences.en: Can we talk about that a little bit?
sentences.zh: 我们能谈谈那个吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Well, there's the medicines and then there's the psychotherapies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有药物治疗，还有心理治疗。

sentences.en: And the medicines that we found are most effective are mood stabilizers and in that category are drugs like lithium, valproic acid or valproate, which is also called Depakote,
sentences.zh: 我们发现最有效的药物是情绪稳定剂，这一类药物包括锂盐、丙戊酸或丙戊酸盐（也叫Depakote），

sentences.en: Lamotrigine, which is also called Lamictal.
sentences.zh: 拉莫三嗪（也叫Lamictal）。

sentences.en: Those are mood stabilizers and they, interestingly, they also have a role in the treatment of epilepsy, at least Lamictal and Depakote do.
sentences.zh: 这些是情绪稳定剂，有趣的是，它们在癫痫治疗中也发挥作用，至少Lamictal和Depakote是这样。

sentences.en: Then we have the antipsychotics, which are drugs like Risperidone, Aripiprazole, Latuda, various drugs that are used really,
sentences.zh: 然后我们有抗精神病药，比如利培酮、阿立哌唑、鲁拉西酮，各种真正被使用的药物，

sentences.en: usually in the acute manic phase to kind of bring someone down from mania.
sentences.zh: 通常在急性躁狂期使用，以使人从躁狂中平复下来。

sentences.en: The person may continue on them for longer to be able to stabilize their symptoms,
sentences.zh: 患者可能会继续服用更长时间，以稳定他们的症状。

sentences.en: but we don't like to have people on those forever because they have side effects like weight gain, fatigue, agitation, sometimes.
sentences.zh: 但我们不喜欢让患者长期服用这些药物，因为它们有时会产生副作用，比如体重增加、疲劳和焦虑。

sentences.en: All these drugs have some side effects.
sentences.zh: 所有这些药物都有一定的副作用。

sentences.en: We do bring in antidepressants once in a while if a person has a very treatment-resistant depression.
sentences.zh: 如果患者的抑郁症对治疗非常顽固，我们偶尔也会引入抗抑郁药。

sentences.en: But the problem with antidepressants, as Terry was alluding to, is they can increase cycling.
sentences.zh: 但正如Terry刚才提到的，抗抑郁药的问题在于它们可能会增加循环发作的频率。

sentences.en: They can cause more rapid cycling, more switches from high to low.
sentences.zh: 它们可能导致更快速的循环，即情绪在高低之间更频繁地切换。

sentences.en: Then there's psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 接下来是心理治疗。

sentences.en: Our particular brand that we've tested in our lab is a family-focused therapy oriented towards functioning within the family,
sentences.zh: 我们在实验室测试过的一种特定疗法是家庭聚焦疗法，旨在改善家庭内部的功能，

sentences.en: getting the family to understand what bipolar disorder is, how to communicate about it, how to be supportive without taking over for the person,
sentences.zh: 让家人了解什么是双相情感障碍，如何就此进行沟通，如何在不越俎代庖的情况下给予支持，

sentences.en: how to encourage medication compliance without being controlling,
sentences.zh: 如何在不进行控制的情况下鼓励患者遵医嘱服药，

sentences.en: how to recognize an early warning sign when it's developing, how to recognize an early warning sign when it's developing, all that can,
sentences.zh: 以及如何在病情发展时识别早期预警信号，所有这些，

sentences.en: the family can be of considerable help in that process.
sentences.zh: 家人在这一过程中可以提供相当大的帮助。

sentences.en: Other people prefer to go the individual route and have an individual therapist who's helping them kind of with their identity formation despite having this disorder or a cognitive behavioral therapist who might work with them on their self-talk or their attributions.
sentences.zh: 有些人更倾向于个人治疗，通过个人治疗师帮助他们在患有这种疾病的情况下进行自我认同的构建，或者通过认知行为治疗师来改善他们的自我对话或归因方式。

sentences.en: Groups, I think, are very useful for people with bipolar disorder, especially if they involve other people who have the disorder and can give them advice on how to cope.
sentences.zh: 我认为小组治疗对双相情感障碍患者非常有用，特别是如果小组成员也患有这种疾病，他们可以提供应对建议。

sentences.en: So most effective treatments are a combination of medications and psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 因此，最有效的治疗方法是药物治疗与心理治疗相结合。

sentences.en: And is that what you're doing, Terry?
sentences.zh: Terry，你现在是这样做的吗？

sentences.en: Are you doing a combination of both?
sentences.zh: 你是在同时进行这两种治疗吗？

sentences.en: And I know you've also written about sort of taking a cocktail of a lot of different drugs over a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 我知道你还写过关于长期服用多种药物组合的文章。

sentences.en: And how do you deal with that?
sentences.zh: 你是如何应对这种情况的？

sentences.en: It can be very difficult to deal with the medication requirement, but I think it is necessary to be on medication if you're bipolar.
sentences.zh: 应对药物需求可能非常困难，但我认为如果你患有双相情感障碍，服药是必要的。

sentences.en: It also, for me, felt less stigmatic to know that there was a medication that could help me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，知道有一种药物可以帮助我，也减轻了我的病耻感。

sentences.en: It felt like, okay, there was something definitively wrong in my brain that could be fixed.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是，好吧，我的大脑确实出了点问题，但它是可以修复的。

sentences.en: And certainly I've been helped tremendously by medication.
sentences.zh: 当然，药物对我帮助巨大。

sentences.en: Although I'd like to add about antipsychotics, that that's a terrifying word for a layperson to hear because I was never psychotic.
sentences.zh: 虽然我想补充一点关于抗精神病药的看法，这个词对外行来说听起来很可怕，因为我从未出现过精神病症状。

sentences.en: But in fact, it turned out to be an antipsychotic eripiprazole that helped me the moSt.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，最终证明阿立哌唑这种抗精神病药对我帮助最大。

sentences.en: So you just have to be open to your doctor's advice.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要对医生的建议保持开放态度即可。

sentences.en: Therapy has been essential for me.
sentences.zh: 治疗对我来说至关重要。

sentences.en: I've been in therapy for 30 years, group therapy, regular therapy, everything that Dr. Miklowitz mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我已经接受了30年的治疗，包括团体治疗、常规治疗，以及Miklowitz博士提到的所有疗法。

sentences.en: I've done it all.
sentences.zh: 我都尝试过。

sentences.en: And I think what I'm discovering now, and I'm doing very well now, is mindfulness is a huge part of my recovery.
sentences.zh: 我现在发现，而且我目前状态很好，正念是我康复过程中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Just learning to try to stay in the moment without too much judgment, without anxiety about the future.
sentences.zh: 学会试着活在当下，减少评判，不再对未来感到焦虑。

sentences.en: It really has been helpful.
sentences.zh: 这确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: Is that a treatment that's becoming more common, Dr. Miklowitz?
sentences.zh: Miklowitz博士，这是一种正变得越来越普遍的治疗方法吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: We've done some studies on it, and others have as well.
sentences.zh: 我们和其他研究人员都对此进行过研究。

sentences.en: Well, mindfulness-based cognitive therapy has been found to be effective for major depression and preventing recurrences of major depression.
sentences.zh: 正念认知疗法已被证明对重度抑郁症有效，并能预防重度抑郁症的复发。

sentences.en: There's some beginning evidence that it might be effective for bipolar disorder as well.
sentences.zh: 目前有一些初步证据表明，它对双相情感障碍也可能有效。

sentences.en: It's not clear that it prevents mania as well as it prevents depression.
sentences.zh: 但尚不清楚它在预防躁狂发作方面是否像预防抑郁发作那样有效。

sentences.en: That's actually what I was going to ask you, Terry, is whether or not you feel like the mindfulness helps during the manic phase as well,
sentences.zh: 这其实正是我要问你的，Terry，你是否觉得正念在躁狂阶段也有帮助，

sentences.en: whether it helps bring you down from a high...
sentences.zh: 它是否能帮你从高涨的情绪中平复下来……

sentences.en: Well, I have an interesting response to that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对此有一个有趣的反应。

sentences.en: I think, actually, that mindfulness makes me so much happier.
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为，正念让我快乐得多。

sentences.en: Sometimes I think I'm hypomanic, which is the state just below mania, where you're feeling terrific, and life is going really well, and you feel on top of your game.
sentences.zh: 有时我觉得自己处于轻躁狂状态，也就是略低于躁狂的状态，那时你感觉棒极了，生活非常顺利，感觉自己处于最佳状态。

sentences.en: So I'm very curious, Dr. Miklowitz, if you've ever heard of mindfulness causing hypomania, or is that just a great side effect I'm experiencing?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，Miklowitz博士，你是否听说过正念会导致轻躁狂，还是说这只是我经历的一个很棒的副作用？

sentences.en: I haven't seen any data on it, but I've heard people say it.
sentences.zh: 我还没有看到任何相关数据，但我确实听人说过。

sentences.en: I've heard people who've been in the groups say that it gives them special insights, and they get very sort of excited about those insights.
sentences.zh: 我听参加过小组的人说，这给了他们特殊的洞察力，他们对这些洞察感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: So I think like any antidepressant, maybe it's like antidepressant medications.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为就像任何抗抑郁药一样，也许它就像抗抑郁药物。

sentences.en: When you improve mood, you also have the risk of setting someone into mania, but there's no data on it.
sentences.zh: 当你改善情绪时，也有可能诱发躁狂，但目前还没有相关数据。

sentences.en: What about other lifestyle factors, such as getting regular sleep or avoiding alcohol?
sentences.zh: 那么其他生活方式因素呢，比如保持规律睡眠或避免饮酒？

sentences.en: Tara, you've talked about how important it is for you to avoid alcohol.
sentences.zh: Tara，你曾谈到避免饮酒对你来说有多重要。

sentences.en: Are there other triggers that you feel you really need to avoid?
sentences.zh: 还有其他你觉得必须避免的诱因吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I've been sober for 23 years, and it wasn't until I stopped drinking that my medications actually began to work.
sentences.zh: 是的，我已经戒酒23年了，直到我停止饮酒，我的药物才开始真正起作用。

sentences.en: And that was a total shock to me because I thought it was just a suggestion that you not drink alcohol and take this drug at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说完全是个震惊，因为我原以为不要同时饮酒和服药只是一条建议而已。

sentences.en: It turned out to be that my brain chemistry just really needed to not have the alcohol interfering with the medication.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，我的大脑化学环境确实需要避免酒精干扰药物作用。

sentences.en: But as far as other lifestyle factors, sleep is critical.
sentences.zh: 至于其他生活方式因素，睡眠至关重要。

sentences.en: Sleep has always been a difficult thing for me with bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 对于双相情感障碍患者来说，睡眠一直是个难题。

sentences.en: But interestingly enough, I found when I went through menopause that when I got on hormonal medications, my sleep improved and my bipolar disorder improved as well.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，我发现进入更年期后，当我开始接受激素治疗时，我的睡眠改善了，双相情感障碍也随之好转。

sentences.en: So it's a thing to check out.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个值得关注的方向。

sentences.en: Now, also, checking on my thyroid has been important.
sentences.zh: 此外，检查甲状腺也很重要。

sentences.en: That can impact my bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 它会影响我的双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: So there are all these interrelated factors.
sentences.zh: 所以这些因素都是相互关联的。

sentences.en: You need to live a healthy lifestyle if you want to be healthy mentally, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果你想保持心理健康，就需要过健康的生活方式。

sentences.en: Can I add to that as well?
sentences.zh: 我能补充一点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, if you would, yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以，请说。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I agree with everything Terry said, and I think everything she said about alcohol could also apply to marijuana.
sentences.zh: 我同意Terry所说的一切，我认为她关于酒精的观点同样适用于大麻。

sentences.en: There are people who smoke weed consistently, and they're thinking it's a mood stabilizer, but actually it can in its own way contribute to your mood cycling, if nothing else,
sentences.zh: 有些人持续吸食大麻，以为它是情绪稳定剂，但实际上它本身就会导致情绪循环，即便没有其他因素，

sentences.en: by interfering with sleep.
sentences.zh: 它也会干扰睡眠。

sentences.en: Some people get high and then they can't fall asleep, or it makes them sort of fatigue during the day, so they take naps.
sentences.zh: 有些人吸食后会兴奋得睡不着，或者导致白天疲劳，不得不午睡。

sentences.en: There are various reasons why any substance of abuse is not a good thing to do when you're also taking psychiatric medications.
sentences.zh: 在服用精神科药物的同时滥用任何物质都是不明智的，原因有很多。

sentences.en: One of the first things we recommend to people with bipolar disorder is to try to stay on a regular sleep-wake cycle, which sounds easy when you say it,
sentences.zh: 我们向双相情感障碍患者推荐的首要建议之一是尝试保持规律的睡眠-觉醒周期，说起来容易，

sentences.en: but it actually is very, very difficult, because first, the disorder interferes with sleep, and it's hard to get to sleep when you have the disorder.
sentences.zh: 但实际上非常非常困难，因为首先，这种疾病本身就会干扰睡眠，患病时很难入睡。

sentences.en: And also, you may be hypomanic, your mind may be going fast, or you may be depressed and find it hard to get through the day without having a nap.
sentences.zh: 而且，你可能处于轻躁狂状态，思维飞速运转，或者处于抑郁状态，不午睡就很难熬过一天。

sentences.en: So, one of the first strategies is to try to get people to have their bedtime within a certain range and their wake-up time within a certain range,
sentences.zh: 因此，首要策略之一是尽量让患者的入睡时间和起床时间保持在一定范围内，

sentences.en: so they don't oversleep or sleep binge, as we call it.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就不会睡过头或出现我们所说的“睡眠暴饮暴食”。

sentences.en: Now, there's an idea that bipolar disorder, particularly the manic phase of bipolar disorder, is linked to creativity and even creative genius.
sentences.zh: 现在有一种观点认为，双相情感障碍，特别是其躁狂阶段，与创造力甚至天才创造力有关。

sentences.en: Is there any truth to that, or is that just a myth?
sentences.zh: 这有道理吗，还是仅仅是个神话？

sentences.en: Do you want to answer that, Terry?
sentences.zh: Terry，你想回答这个问题吗？

sentences.en: I'd like to jump in and say, I think there's an absolute connection.
sentences.zh: 我想插一句，我认为绝对存在这种联系。

sentences.en: I have known many, many bipolar people over the course of my publishing career,
sentences.zh: 在我的出版生涯中，我认识许多许多双相情感障碍患者，

sentences.en: and certainly there is a connection in my mind to artistry and just bipolar disorder in general, not necessarily mania,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，艺术天赋与双相情感障碍之间确实存在联系，不一定是躁狂，

sentences.en: but there are things that happen when you're bipolar that give you an extra edge when you're an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 但当你患有双相情感障碍时，确实会发生一些事情，让你在从事艺术创作时拥有额外的优势。

sentences.en: You develop a great deal of empathy because you've suffered so much, and so you can bring that to your art.
sentences.zh: 你因为遭受了太多的痛苦而培养出了极强的同理心，所以你可以将其带入你的艺术创作中。

sentences.en: And I think you also are somewhat of an outsider when you're bipolar, and that allows you to watch people and, you know, trying to find out what's a normal behavior.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为当你患有双相情感障碍时，你多少有点局外人的感觉，这让你能够观察他人，试图找出什么是正常行为。

sentences.en: And that also helps with creativity.
sentences.zh: 这也对创造力有帮助。

sentences.en: So I think there's a lot of that being bipolar that is connected to creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为双相情感障碍中有很多方面与创造力有关。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I would agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我也同意这一点。

sentences.en: Certainly there is many historical figures who've had bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 历史上确实有很多患有双相情感障碍的名人。

sentences.en: At least when we look back, it certainly looks like they had bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 至少当我们回顾过去时，他们看起来确实患有双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: Various painters, Tchaikovsky, the classic musician, Beethoven, we think, probably had bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 各种画家，柴可夫斯基，古典音乐家，贝多芬，我们认为可能都患有双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: Kurt Cobain, you know, more recently had probably had bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: Kurt Cobain，你知道的，最近的例子，可能也患有双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: And the linkage, though, we think it may be that people create more during hypomania than mania, because it certainly helps you to speed up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 不过我们认为，这种联系可能在于人们在轻躁狂时比在躁狂时创作更多，因为它确实能帮你加快一点节奏。

sentences.en: Your thoughts go faster, and you kind of think outside the box a little bit more when you're hypomanic.
sentences.zh: 你的思维变快了，在轻躁狂时，你的思维也会更跳脱一些。

sentences.en: But when you get manic, I don't know if Terry would agree with this, but I think people produce a lot of work, but it's not their best work.
sentences.zh: 但当你进入躁狂状态时，我不知道Terry是否同意这一点，但我认为人们虽然产出很多作品，但那并不是他们最好的作品。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I'd agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我同意这一点。

sentences.en: When I'm hypomanic, I see connections between things.
sentences.zh: 当我处于轻躁狂状态时，我能看到事物之间的联系。

sentences.en: It's astonishing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: It's like the fabric of the universe just seems to be connected, and it makes sense to me.
sentences.zh: 感觉宇宙的结构仿佛连接在一起，对我来说一切都说得通。

sentences.en: And I'm able to write about that.
sentences.zh: 我能够写下这些内容。

sentences.en: But when I'm manic, I think I have all these fabulous, grandiose ideas, and I put them down on paper.
sentences.zh: 但当我处于躁狂状态时，我觉得自己有了所有这些美妙、宏大的想法，并把它们写在纸上。

sentences.en: And it's usually in the tiniest imaginable little script that I can't decipher later when I'm not manic.
sentences.zh: 通常是用我能想象到的最小的字迹写出来的，等我不再躁狂时就无法辨认了。

sentences.en: So most of my manic writing has gone out the window.
sentences.zh: 所以我大部分躁狂时期的作品都作废了。

sentences.en: So is it a goal then to basically titrate the medicine so that you can sort of keep at that hypo level because it's effective?
sentences.zh: 那么，目标是否基本上是调整药物剂量，让你保持在轻躁狂水平，因为它很有效？

sentences.en: That's something that Kay Jamieson has written a lot about is her.
sentences.zh: Kay Jamieson写过很多关于这方面的内容。

sentences.en: She was a psychologist and also a writer.
sentences.zh: 她是一位心理学家，也是一位作家。

sentences.en: She talked about finding the sort of optimal level of lithium that allowed her some hypomania but still protected against recurrences.
sentences.zh: 她谈到了寻找锂盐的最佳水平，既能让她保持一定的轻躁狂，又能防止复发。

sentences.en: And that is a balancing act.
sentences.zh: 这是一种平衡的艺术。

sentences.en: It's different for different people.
sentences.zh: 对不同的人来说情况不同。

sentences.en: You have to get your doctor on board with having, you know, can I take a lower lithium level?
sentences.zh: 你必须让你的医生同意，比如，我能降低锂盐剂量吗？

sentences.en: But for some people who are artists, that's very critical to be able to make that balance.
sentences.zh: 但对于一些艺术家来说，能够实现这种平衡至关重要。

sentences.en: Terri, I saw that you wrote about how you believe your bipolar disorder has led you to being very circumscribed in your movements, especially when you're feeling depressed.
sentences.zh: Terry，我看到你写过，你认为你的双相情感障碍导致你的行动非常受限，尤其是在你感到抑郁的时候。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Like, what is that like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And how did you discover that you were sort of different in that respect?
sentences.zh: 你是如何发现自己在这一方面与众不同的？

sentences.en: Oh, Kim,
sentences.zh: 哦，Kim，

sentences.en: I'm so glad you brought that up because that's something that I have written about frequently and I've gotten the most responses to that subject because I think many people are suffering from what is called psychomotor retardation,
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你提到了这一点，因为这是我经常写到的主题，也是我收到回应最多的主题，因为我认为许多人正在遭受所谓的“精神运动性迟滞”的折磨，

sentences.en: a slowing down of the mental and physical processes of the body in depression.
sentences.zh: 即抑郁症中身心过程的减缓。

sentences.en: And it is terrifying.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: It's like a paralysis.
sentences.zh: 这就像瘫痪一样。

sentences.en: If I were to, I'm sitting at my desk right now and I want to reach out and grab my pen, I couldn't do that.
sentences.zh: 如果我现在坐在桌前，想伸手去拿笔，我做不到。

sentences.en: I'd have to think about it and think about it and ponder it and my hands still would not obey my mind.
sentences.zh: 我必须思考、思考、再思考，但我的手依然不听使唤。

sentences.en: That's psychomotor retardation.
sentences.zh: 这就是精神运动性迟滞。

sentences.en: And I think it really does not get the amount of attention that it should because I have been helped by psychostimulants with that and I think other people could be as well and Dr. Miklowitz could address that.
sentences.zh: 我认为它没有得到应有的关注，因为我曾通过精神兴奋剂得到过缓解，我认为其他人也可以，Miklowitz博士可以谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: But it really is for me the worst part of being bipolar.
sentences.zh: 但这对我来说确实是患双相情感障碍最糟糕的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I wondered, actually, I was going to ask you this earlier, Terry, does that extend to getting out of bed in the morning?
sentences.zh: 是的，我其实之前就想问你，Terry，这种情况会延伸到早晨起床吗？

sentences.en: Do you find that when you're depressed, it's very difficult to even move out of bed?
sentences.zh: 你是否发现当你抑郁时，甚至连起床都非常困难？

sentences.en: I live in my bed.
sentences.zh: 我住在床上。

sentences.en: When I'm depressed, I don't go much further than the kitchen or the bathroom.
sentences.zh: 当我抑郁时，我不会去离厨房或浴室太远的地方。

sentences.en: But the bed becomes my universe, unfortunately, because you simply can't get the comforter off.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，床成了我的宇宙，因为你根本无法掀开被子。

sentences.en: It's too heavy.
sentences.zh: 它太沉了。

sentences.en: Have you found any effective treatments for that particular problem?
sentences.zh: 你有没有发现针对这个特定问题的有效治疗方法？

sentences.en: When it's really severe depression, nothing helps but time.
sentences.zh: 当抑郁非常严重时，除了时间，什么都没用。

sentences.en: But when it's not quite as bad, again, I've found that psychostimulants have been helpful, like modafinil helps me.
sentences.zh: 但当情况没那么糟糕时，我发现精神兴奋剂很有帮助，比如莫达非尼对我有效。

sentences.en: Sometimes Ritalin can be helpful or a combination of all of those, along with my mood stabilizers and my antidepressants.
sentences.zh: 有时利他林也有帮助，或者将它们与我的情绪稳定剂和抗抑郁药结合使用。

sentences.en: So I have found some help with the medication, but I wish someone could help with the terror of it returning, because, again, it is the worst part of being bipolar.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实从药物中找到了一些帮助，但我希望有人能帮我解决那种恐惧感，因为它确实是患双相情感障碍最糟糕的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think one of the things families struggle with most is they say, well, if you would just get out of bed, you'd be fine.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为家庭最纠结的一点是他们会说，如果你能起床，你就会好起来的。

sentences.en: And if you would just, you know, kind of make yourself do things, you know, you'll be a lot happier.
sentences.zh: 如果你能强迫自己做点事，你会快乐得多。

sentences.en: Yet, what they don't get is that when you wake up with bipolar disorder, it's like having a 100-pound weight on your cheSt.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们不明白的是，当你患有双相情感障碍醒来时，就像胸口压着一百磅的重物。

sentences.en: You can't move, even if you want to, even if you feel like you should.
sentences.zh: 你动弹不得，即使你想动，即使你觉得你应该动。

sentences.en: It's a physical state that's very difficult to overcome, and it's hard for family members to understand that.
sentences.zh: 这是一种很难克服的生理状态，家人很难理解这一点。

sentences.en: They say, well, I got up this morning.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我今天早上就起床了。

sentences.en: How come you can't?
sentences.zh: 你怎么就起不来呢？

sentences.en: But it is a serious physiological limitation that's brought on by depression.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是由抑郁症引起的严重的生理限制。

sentences.en: And that brings me back to family-focused therapy.
sentences.zh: 这让我想回到家庭聚焦疗法的话题。

sentences.en: I mean, what are some of the techniques that you use when you do this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在进行这种治疗时使用的一些技巧是什么？

sentences.en: Because that's got to be something that is very hard for the patient to hear when, you know, mom and dad are saying, just get out of bed, kiddo.
sentences.zh: 因为当父母对孩子说“孩子，快起床”时，这对患者来说一定很难听进去。

sentences.en: And it's like, the kid can't get out of bed.
sentences.zh: 就像是，孩子根本起不来。

sentences.en: So, I mean, how do you walk the family through that and get the parents to be helpful and understanding?
sentences.zh: 所以，你是如何引导家庭度过这一关，让父母变得更有帮助和理解力的呢？

sentences.en: I think anytime you hear a criticism like that, you have to think about it in a couple of different ways.
sentences.zh: 我认为当你听到这样的批评时，你必须从几个不同的角度去思考它。

sentences.en: You can't just wag your finger at the parents and say, don't criticize.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是对父母指手画脚，说“不要批评”。

sentences.en: You have to say, first, their intention is a good one.
sentences.zh: 你得先说，他们的初衷是好的。

sentences.en: Their intention is that they want the kid to be happier.
sentences.zh: 他们的初衷是希望孩子能更快乐。

sentences.en: They want him to be healthier.
sentences.zh: 他们希望孩子更健康。

sentences.en: They want him to get or her to get out of bed and be able to finish school.
sentences.zh: 他们希望孩子能起床，能完成学业。

sentences.en: But the way they're communicating it is in a way that's just going to feel invalidating to the child.
sentences.zh: 但他们沟通的方式，只会让孩子感到被否定。

sentences.en: And then we'll work with them on what, you know, let's first let's understand why she has this problem getting up in the morning.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们会和他们一起探讨，比如，我们先来了解为什么她早上起床会有困难。

sentences.en: Uh, that's the nature of the illness.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是疾病的本质。

sentences.en: Other people who have this disorder have that same problem.
sentences.zh: 其他患有这种疾病的人也有同样的问题。

sentences.en: Let's set some smaller goals.
sentences.zh: 让我们设定一些更小的目标。

sentences.en: Like, can she get up within this interval, within this hour of time?
sentences.zh: 比如，她能在某个时间段内，比如这一小时内起床吗？

sentences.en: If she's a little late to school, is that, can we work it out with the school to, uh, accept that or to not, you know, dock her every time she shows up late to school?
sentences.zh: 如果她上学迟到了一点，我们能不能和学校协商一下，接受这种情况，或者不要每次她迟到都扣分？

sentences.en: Are there adjustments to medications that can be made, uh, taking them earlier?
sentences.zh: 药物方面是否可以调整，比如早点服用？

sentences.en: Or, for example, uh, in the day, the previous day, so that she doesn't have the sleep inertia in the morning.
sentences.zh: 或者，比如在前一天，这样她早上就不会有睡眠惯性了。

sentences.en: That's, that's problem solving with the family, really.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正与家庭一起解决问题。

sentences.en: And also getting them to understand what it's like from the child's or the young adult's perspective, uh, and how to communicate about it.
sentences.zh: 同时也要让他们理解孩子或年轻人的视角，以及如何进行沟通。

sentences.en: Yeah, I, I would love to, I'd love to jump in there, Dr. Miklowitz, because, um, I know from my own experience
sentences.zh: 是的，我非常想插一句，Miklowitz 博士，因为根据我自己的经验，

sentences.en: that any type of advice is going to come off as criticism when you're depressed, because
sentences.zh: 当你抑郁时，任何建议听起来都像是批评，因为

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Anyone who says you should do this, my God, if I could, wouldn't I be doing it?
sentences.zh: 任何说“你应该这样做”的人，天哪，如果我能做到，我难道不会去做吗？

sentences.en: Um, no one wants to be lying there trapped by their comforter.
sentences.zh: 没人想躺在那里被被子困住。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, but I have a suggestion for how to communicate that I've written about, and I feel very strongly about, which you were just referencing.
sentences.zh: 不过，我有一个关于沟通的建议，我写过相关内容，也深信不疑，这正是你刚才提到的。

sentences.en: It's understanding what the person is going through by just five little words.
sentences.zh: 只需五个字，就能理解对方正在经历什么。

sentences.en: Tell me where it hurts.
sentences.zh: 告诉我哪里痛。

sentences.en: Tell me where it hurts.
sentences.zh: 告诉我哪里痛。

sentences.en: If you say that to a person and you let them open up and explain about how they're feeling in the darkness and the paralysis, it shifts something in the relationship.
sentences.zh: 如果你对一个人这样说，让他们敞开心扉，解释他们在黑暗和瘫痪感中的感受，这会改变人际关系中的某些东西。

sentences.en: And also in the depressed person's, uh, sense of being all alone with their disease.
sentences.zh: 也会改变抑郁者那种独自面对疾病的孤独感。

sentences.en: It's, I've seen it work countless times and it certainly does work for me.
sentences.zh: 我见过无数次这种方法奏效，它对我确实有效。

sentences.en: Just tell me where it hurts.
sentences.zh: 只要告诉我哪里痛。

sentences.en: And then you've got to listen.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须倾听。

sentences.en: That's the hard part and not try to make it all better.
sentences.zh: 这是最难的部分，不要试图让一切好起来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I guess the flip side of that is the person with the disorder has to also be willing to understand the confusion their parents are going through.
sentences.zh: 我想这反过来说，患病者也必须愿意理解父母所经历的困惑。

sentences.en: You know, they last, last year, this time you were doing great.
sentences.zh: 你知道，去年这个时候你还做得很好。

sentences.en: How come now this year you can't get out of bed?
sentences.zh: 为什么今年你连床都起不来了？

sentences.en: Uh, some parents reject the idea of an illness.
sentences.zh: 有些父母拒绝承认这是一种疾病。

sentences.en: You know, this can't be an illness.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，这不可能是病。

sentences.en: This is just laziness.
sentences.zh: 这只是懒惰。

sentences.en: You're not trying hard enough.
sentences.zh: 你不够努力。

sentences.en: And although that's not, certainly not helpful to the person with the disorder,
sentences.zh: 虽然这对患者来说肯定没有帮助，

sentences.en: parents are kind of going through their own journey and trying to understand what's wrong with their kid.
sentences.zh: 但父母也在经历他们自己的心路历程，试图理解孩子出了什么问题。

sentences.en: Well, my parents didn't believe I had bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的父母不相信我患有双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: And unfortunately they died before really there was a kind of awareness there is today about it.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他们在当今社会对这种病有一定认知之前就去世了。

sentences.en: But, um, I think this is where education comes in.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这就是教育发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: There is no excuse for everybody not knowing the symptoms and the signs and think simple things like you're going to have trouble getting out of bed.
sentences.zh: 每个人都没有理由不去了解症状和迹象，以及像“起床困难”这样简单的事情。

sentences.en: Um, there are so many books now about bipolar disorder and so many great, well, there's this podcast and there's so many great examples of education out there.
sentences.zh: 现在有太多关于双相情感障碍的书籍，还有很多很棒的资源，比如这个播客，以及很多优秀的教育案例。

sentences.en: Or you just have to go to the internet and start learning the symptoms and the signs and the triggers.
sentences.zh: 或者你只需要上网，开始学习症状、迹象和诱因。

sentences.en: And yet it's so, it's hard to, to diagnose.
sentences.zh: 然而，诊断确实很难。

sentences.en: I mean, Dr. McLeod, can you talk about why it's so hard to diagnose?
sentences.zh: McLeod 博士，你能谈谈为什么诊断这么难吗？

sentences.en: Because I mean, it sounds like a pretty clear cut syndrome.
sentences.zh: 因为听起来这似乎是一个非常明确的综合征。

sentences.en: So if the person has a clear cut manic episode, alternating with clear cut depressive episodes, it's not that hard to diagnose.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人有明确的躁狂发作，并与明确的抑郁发作交替出现，诊断起来并不难。

sentences.en: It's, you can get the history, you can hear, you know, go through a checklist of symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 你可以获取病史，过一遍症状清单。

sentences.en: Do they have five of those symptoms?
sentences.zh: 他们有其中的五种症状吗？

sentences.en: Have they lasted this amount of time?
sentences.zh: 它们持续了这么长时间吗？

sentences.en: And you have your diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 然后你就有了诊断结果。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, most people present in a much more ambiguous way than that.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，大多数人的表现要模糊得多。

sentences.en: They have manic and depressive symptoms at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他们同时有躁狂和抑郁症状。

sentences.en: They have short episodes alternating with longer episodes.
sentences.zh: 他们的短发作与长发作交替出现。

sentences.en: They have hypomanias, sometimes in manias at other times.
sentences.zh: 有时是轻躁狂，有时是躁狂。

sentences.en: They have depressions that have some psychotic features.
sentences.zh: 他们的抑郁症伴有一些精神病性特征。

sentences.en: They also have ADHD and therefore can't tell what part of this is hyperactive behavior due to the ADHD and what part of it is mania.
sentences.zh: 他们还有多动症（ADHD），因此无法分辨哪些是多动症引起的多动行为，哪些是躁狂。

sentences.en: Or they have severe anxiety, which can look an awful lot like manic overstimulated thinking.
sentences.zh: 或者他们有严重的焦虑症，看起来很像躁狂导致的过度刺激思维。

sentences.en: So there's so many things that look like it.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多看起来像它的东西。

sentences.en: You have to take your time to do a diagnostic interview, a full diagnostic assessment.
sentences.zh: 你必须花时间进行诊断访谈，进行全面的诊断评估。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, the mental health system doesn't always allow for that.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，心理健康系统并不总是允许这样做。

sentences.en: And also, I think it's essential to have family input.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为获得家庭的反馈至关重要。

sentences.en: And I'm sure Dr. Michalowicz agrees because you need to see a pattern emerging over time.
sentences.zh: 我相信 Miklowitz 博士也会同意，因为你需要观察随时间推移出现的模式。

sentences.en: And the best person for that or the best people for that are friends and family to really talk to the doctor and say, well, three months ago,
sentences.zh: 而最适合做这件事的人就是朋友和家人，他们可以真正与医生沟通，说，嗯，三个月前，

sentences.en: she was talking so fast I couldn't understand her.
sentences.zh: 她说话太快了，我根本听不懂。

sentences.en: You know, little clues like that are really what doctors need, I think.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为医生真正需要的就是这些小线索。

sentences.en: How did you finally get an accurate diagnosis, Terry?
sentences.zh: Terry，你是怎么最终得到准确诊断的？

sentences.en: What would it take for that to happen?
sentences.zh: 这需要什么条件？

sentences.en: I had such bad depression that I had electroshock therapy.
sentences.zh: 我当时抑郁得非常严重，以至于接受了电休克治疗。

sentences.en: The depression was so severe.
sentences.zh: 抑郁程度太深了。

sentences.en: And in the middle of electroshock therapy, I escalated into the highest bad of mania I'd ever had.
sentences.zh: 在电休克治疗期间，我陷入了我经历过的最严重的躁狂状态。

sentences.en: I spent every last cent I owned.
sentences.zh: 我花光了所有的积蓄。

sentences.en: And I went up the coast to a five-star resort and just stayed there until my savings account was dry.
sentences.zh: 我去了海岸边的一个五星级度假村，一直待到存款耗尽。

sentences.en: I had a terrific time, but I had to come back and face the consequences, which was not so great.
sentences.zh: 我玩得很开心，但回来后不得不面对后果，那可不太好。

sentences.en: So it took my doctors seeing that and seeing, oh, yeah, I guess she gets manic.
sentences.zh: 所以我的医生看到了这一点，意识到，哦，是的，我想她确实会躁狂。

sentences.en: So maybe she's bipolar.
sentences.zh: 所以也许她是双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: That's what made the difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是转折点。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Michalowicz, I want to ask you, what are the areas of research that you're most excited about right now in terms of improving treatment for people with bipolar disorder?
sentences.zh: 那么，Miklowitz 博士，我想问您，在改善双相情感障碍患者的治疗方面，您目前最看好哪些研究领域？

sentences.en: What are the big questions that you would like to see answered?
sentences.zh: 您最想看到哪些重大问题的答案？

sentences.en: First, we're getting more and more interested in early intervention and prevention.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们对早期干预和预防越来越感兴趣。

sentences.en: If we can catch kids early enough, we're just showing the early warning signs, particularly those who have a family history of the disorder.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能尽早发现孩子的问题，特别是有家族病史的孩子，并观察到早期预警信号，

sentences.en: We may be able to, if not prevent it, minimize the severity.
sentences.zh: 我们也许能够减轻其严重程度，如果不能预防的话。

sentences.en: And so we're going in with family psychoeducation for kids who are showing some manic symptoms, some depressive symptoms, and where bipolar disorder runs in the family.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在对表现出一些躁狂症状、抑郁症状且有双相情感障碍家族史的孩子进行家庭心理教育。

sentences.en: We've been able to show we can prevent depressive episodes or at least elongate the periods of wellness between mood episodes.
sentences.zh: 我们已经能够证明，我们可以预防抑郁发作，或者至少延长情绪发作之间的健康期。

sentences.en: Others have shown the same thing, that early intervention may be one way to at least mollify the course of the disorder over time.
sentences.zh: 其他人也证明了同样的事情，即早期干预可能是缓解疾病长期病程的一种方式。

sentences.en: We're also interested in the whole question of who gets better over time.
sentences.zh: 我们也对“谁会随着时间推移好转”这一整个问题很感兴趣。

sentences.en: We have a subgroup of kids.
sentences.zh: 我们有一组孩子。

sentences.en: It's about 25 or 30 percent of the kids that we see in our clinic who start off and they look bipolar at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 在我们诊所看到的这些孩子中，大约有 25% 到 30% 的人起初看起来像是双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: And by the time they're in their early 20s or late teens, they're pretty stable, even when they're not taking medications.
sentences.zh: 但到了 20 岁出头或十几岁末，他们即使不吃药也相当稳定。

sentences.en: I don't know why that is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么会这样。

sentences.en: That's something I'd like to know.
sentences.zh: 这是我想知道的。

sentences.en: But other shops are finding that as well, that there's a subgroup that have a good outcome.
sentences.zh: 但其他机构也发现了这一点，即确实存在一组预后良好的亚群。

sentences.en: Maybe it's protective factors.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为保护性因素。

sentences.en: Maybe we had the diagnosis wrong in the first place.
sentences.zh: 也许我们一开始就诊断错了。

sentences.en: Or maybe they had a good relationship that protected them against mood variability.
sentences.zh: 或者也许他们有良好的关系，保护他们免受情绪波动的影响。

sentences.en: Those are things that we need to know.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们需要了解的事情。

sentences.en: The other thing we're doing that I'm excited about is we've developed a child bipolar network, which is five or six different university sites.
sentences.zh: 我们正在做的另一件让我感到兴奋的事情是，我们建立了一个儿童双相情感障碍网络，由五六个不同的大学站点组成。

sentences.en: We're trying to put together common diagnostic and treatment guidelines for these kids.
sentences.zh: 我们正在尝试为这些孩子制定共同的诊断和治疗指南。

sentences.en: Like, what do you do when you have a kid who looks bipolar, but the manic episode is due to antidepressants?
sentences.zh: 比如，当一个孩子看起来像双相情感障碍，但躁狂发作是由抗抑郁药引起时，该怎么办？

sentences.en: How do you treat those kids versus somebody who has a longstanding bipolar disorder or has these mixed episodes?
sentences.zh: 如何治疗这些孩子，与那些患有长期双相情感障碍或有混合发作的人相比，有什么不同？

sentences.en: If we could all diagnose kids and treat them the same way, I think we'd be much further along or have a series of guidelines that everyone agrees upon.
sentences.zh: 如果我们都能以同样的方式诊断和治疗孩子，我想我们会进步得多，或者拥有一套大家都认同的指南。

sentences.en: Last word, Terry, I'm going to ask from your vantage point, what would you like to see science and research illuminate, figure out, understand,
sentences.zh: 最后，Terry，我想从你的角度问一下，你希望科学和研究能阐明、弄清、理解，

sentences.en: and essentially resolve for people who are living with bipolar disorder?
sentences.zh: 并从根本上为那些患有双相情感障碍的人解决什么问题？

sentences.en: Well, I have a whole basket full of dreams about that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对此有一大堆梦想。

sentences.en: I would love to know more about psychedelics for bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 我很想了解更多关于迷幻药治疗双相情感障碍的信息。

sentences.en: That really hasn't been explored much yet.
sentences.zh: 这方面目前还没有得到太多探索。

sentences.en: I think there's great promise in the field of psychedelics.
sentences.zh: 我认为迷幻药领域非常有前景。

sentences.en: I think mindfulness also and its application to bipolar disorder could really help people.
sentences.zh: 我认为正念及其在双相情感障碍中的应用也能真正帮助人们。

sentences.en: I'd like more addressing of the cost of medication.
sentences.zh: 我希望更多地解决药物成本问题。

sentences.en: It's killing me.
sentences.zh: 这快把我逼死了。

sentences.en: I'm sure it's killing other people out there.
sentences.zh: 我相信其他人也一样。

sentences.en: I am just on the edge of being not able to afford my medications, and it's very frightening.
sentences.zh: 我正处于买不起药的边缘，这非常可怕。

sentences.en: So I would like to see that researched and addressed.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望看到这方面得到研究和解决。

sentences.en: And I'd like to see the stigma of having bipolar disorder reduced simply because it's not that bad a thing.
sentences.zh: 我还希望看到针对双相情感障碍的污名化能减少，因为它并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: It's not like you're a terrible person.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你是一个糟糕的人。

sentences.en: You're normal, quote, normal in between episodes.
sentences.zh: 在发作间期，你是“正常”的。

sentences.en: You're not always manic or always depressed.
sentences.zh: 你不会总是躁狂或总是抑郁。

sentences.en: You're just a human being with a brain that is hypersensitive to certain things and needs to be addressed by medication.
sentences.zh: 你只是一个人类，大脑对某些事物高度敏感，需要通过药物来调节。

sentences.en: So it really is not that they shouldn't be getting the stigma that it does.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们真的不应该承受现在的这种污名。

sentences.en: I agree with that 100 percent.
sentences.zh: 我百分之百同意这一点。

sentences.en: And also the issue about psychedelics, that is something we're interested in as well.
sentences.zh: 关于迷幻药的问题，这也是我们感兴趣的。

sentences.en: Right now, psychedelics are only being used with major depression.
sentences.zh: 目前，迷幻药仅用于重度抑郁症。

sentences.en: They're not being used for bipolar disorder for what I think are obvious reasons.
sentences.zh: 它们没有被用于双相情感障碍，原因我认为很明显。

sentences.en: You don't want to kick off in a manic episode.
sentences.zh: 你不想引发躁狂发作。

sentences.en: But I think there is a future for that kind of research, both with ketamine.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这类研究是有未来的，无论是氯胺酮还是其他。

sentences.en: Psilocybin has been proposed.
sentences.zh: 裸盖菇素也被提出来了。

sentences.en: And it may be that a single or two sessions of that kind of drug can break through some barriers that people have in terms of their thinking, their ruminations and so on.
sentences.zh: 也许一两次这种药物的疗程就能打破人们在思维、反刍等方面的一些障碍。

sentences.en: I don't think it's a miracle.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是奇迹。

sentences.en: But I think we haven't studied it enough by any means.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们绝对还没有对其进行足够的研究。

sentences.en: Well, it sounds like we've come a long way, but I would certainly have a very long way yet to go.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听起来我们已经走了很长一段路，但肯定还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: I want to thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们今天加入我。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I appreciate particularly, Terry, you're putting yourself out there with your story because it's very, very compelling.
sentences.zh: Terry，我特别感谢你分享自己的故事，因为它非常非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: Thank you also, Dr. Miklitz.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你，Miklowitz 博士。

sentences.en: You're quite welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Kim。

sentences.en: I really appreciate your having me here.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你邀请我来这里。

sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或 Apple、Stitcher 以及您获取播客的任何地方找到《Speaking of Psychology》往期节目。

sentences.zh: 也欢迎给我们留下评论。

sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。
